causes.label: Coolant temperature sensor not connected, connector or wire open
Wrong module software or variant
Faulty sensor
Internal module fault

symptoms: Check engine light
Radiator fan runs constantly
Temperature gauge not working
Poor cold start, higher consumption

P0640.title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
P0640.description: Some diesels (for example GM's 6.6 L Duramax LML and the Cummins in Ram trucks) warm the intake air with a heater grid switched by a relay or semiconductor switch. P0640 reports a fault in its control circuit. GM's LML glow plug module expects a digital feedback from the heater while it is commanded on; if it is missing for 2 s (75 % of 4 s), the code sets and the lamp follows after two trips. Current, voltage and temperature faults run under GM's own codes P154A–P154D. CARB requires intake air heaters to be checked for response, current and voltage drop. The result is poor cold starts, white smoke and rough running after a cold start; a relay stuck on drains the battery – Ram recalled 2021 trucks because a shorted heater relay could overheat. Ford's 2023 diesel does not use P0640.

causes.label: Heater relay or switching module faulty
Control wire or connector open or corroded
Heater grid burnt out or shorted to ground
Heater main cable or fuse loose or faulty
Glow plug or engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light
Poor cold start in low temperatures
White smoke, rough running after cold start
Flat battery if the relay sticks

P0641.title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit/Open
P0641.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (pedal, throttle, pressure and position sensors) from shared, regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'A' is circuit 1. A short on one sensor or its wire pulls down every sensor on that circuit and triggers many follow-up codes – so look for the one faulty sensor or chafed wire, for example by unplugging the sensors one at a time. P0641 is the general code for circuit A. GM puts everything into this one code: reference outside 4.875–5.125 V or jumping (filtered against unfiltered value), 19 of 39 counts or 0.19 s in a row, lamp in the first trip; circuits 2–4 are P0651, P0697 and P06A3, and GM does not use P0642/P0643. GM Europe's 2.0 L diesel flags it outside 4.5–5.5 V for 0.5 s with reduced engine power (two trips), the 2.0 L petrol after 1 s or 10 s cumulative (first trip). Because throttle and pedal sensors may be affected, limp mode is common.

causes.label: Short to ground or voltage at one of the supplied sensors or its wire
A sensor signal wire shorted to voltage
Harness damage (chafing, rodent bite, water in connector)
Module internal (reference regulator)

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode with reduced power
Many codes from several sensors at once
Possibly starting or boost problems

P0642.title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit Low
P0642.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (pedal, throttle, pressure and position sensors) from shared, regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'A' is circuit 1. A short on one sensor or its wire pulls down every sensor on that circuit and triggers many follow-up codes – so look for the one faulty sensor or chafed wire, for example by unplugging the sensors one at a time. P0642 means the voltage of reference circuit A is too low – typically the 5 V wire or a connected sensor is shorted to ground. Ford checks continuously from ignition on and sets it below 4.75 V after 5 s; GM Europe's 2.0 L petrol after 1 s or 10 s cumulative, lamp in the first trip. GM North America reports it as P0641. All sensors on the circuit then read near 0 V, with matching 'low' codes. High is P0643, range/performance P06A6.

causes.label: 5 V wire or sensor shorted to ground
Internal short in a supplied sensor (e.g. pressure sensor)
Chafed harness or water ingress
Module reference regulator faulty

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode with reduced power
Many codes from several sensors at once
Possibly starting or boost problems

P0643.title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit High
P0643.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (pedal, throttle, pressure and position sensors) from shared, regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'A' is circuit 1. A short on one sensor or its wire pulls down every sensor on that circuit and triggers many follow-up codes – so look for the one faulty sensor or chafed wire, for example by unplugging the sensors one at a time. P0643 means the voltage of reference circuit A is too high – the 5 V wire is shorted to battery voltage or to a higher potential, for example a sensor signal wire shorted to voltage. Ford sets it above 5.25 V after 5 s; GM Europe's 2.0 L petrol after 1 s or 10 s cumulative, lamp in the first trip; GM North America reports it as P0641. Sensors then read too high, and battery voltage on the reference can damage them. Low is P0642.

causes.label: 5 V wire shorted to battery voltage
Signal wire of a supplied sensor shorted to voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode with reduced power
Several 'high' sensor codes
Implausible readings (pressure, pedal)

P0644.title: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit
P0644.description: P0644 concerns a dedicated serial line on which the engine module sends values or warnings to a driver display or information display – not the general vehicle CAN bus. The module reports missing or invalid communication on that line (open, short, display not answering); CARB requires digital outputs to be checked for communication faults. GM Europe's 2010 Saab, for example, passes engine data such as fuel level over CAN to the body module and on to the instrument unit and information display – where such data runs on the bus, a failure is reported as a U code (e.g. U0155) instead. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. Displays then show missing, frozen or jumping information; the engine runs normally.

causes.label: Wire or connector between module and receiver open, corroded or shorted
Display or instrument cluster faulty or without supply (fuse, ground)
Low system voltage during cranking
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Warning message or lamp (depending on the maker)
Information in the driver display missing, frozen or jumping
Display stays dark

P0645.title: A/C Clutch Relay Control Circuit
P0645.description: The engine module switches the A/C compressor clutch relay through a low-side driver once the climate control requests cooling. P0645 is the general circuit fault of the relay coil control, usually an open circuit. GM Europe's 2011 Saab 9-5 sets P0645/P0646 for an open or short to ground and P0647 for a short to voltage, with the engine running and A/C requested; Ford's commercial trucks report it without the check engine light. Older Saab diesels (Bosch EDC16/PSG16) use a different assignment (P0645 short to voltage, 0.6 s). GM found a no-start with P0645 on the 2002–04 Alero/Grand Am 3.4 L because a shorted compressor clutch coil blew a fuse shared with the engine control; Ford traced warm air with P0645 on the 2020–23 Explorer to spread terminals at the body module. The compressor then does not engage or runs constantly.

causes.label: A/C clutch relay faulty (coil open)
Control wire or connector open, terminals spread
Relay or clutch supply fuse blown (e.g. shorted clutch coil)
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: A/C not cooling (compressor does not engage)
Compressor runs constantly
Check engine light usually off, code stored only
Rarely no start if a shared fuse has blown (GM 3.4 L)

P0646.title: A/C Clutch Relay Control Circuit Low
P0646.description: The engine module switches the A/C compressor clutch relay through a low-side driver once the climate control requests cooling. P0646 means the voltage at the control output is too low while the driver is off – the control wire is shorted to ground, so the relay can pull in permanently and the compressor keeps running, which can ice up the evaporator. Saab's EDC16 diesels set it after more than 0.6 s with the engine running; GM Europe's 2011 Saab 9-5 also includes an open circuit here. Ford's OBD summaries list P0646/P0647 in a 5 V reference section for Bosch modules – an unusual assignment not covered here. The code is not emission relevant and does not light the check engine lamp at most makers.

causes.label: Control wire between relay and module shorted to ground (chafing)
Relay faulty internally (coil, ground)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: A/C compressor runs constantly, even with A/C off
Evaporator ices up, cooling drops
With an open circuit: no cooling

P0647.title: A/C Clutch Relay Control Circuit High
P0647.description: The engine module switches the A/C compressor clutch relay through a low-side driver once the climate control requests cooling. P0647 means the voltage at the control output stays too high while the driver switches on (it should pull to ground) – the control wire is shorted to voltage; the driver shuts off for protection and the relay does not pull in, so there is no cooling. GM Europe's 2011 Saab 9-5 uses P0647 only for a short to voltage (check: less than 0.3 V on the control wire with ignition on and the module unplugged); Saab's EDC16 diesels use it for an open circuit instead (0.6 s). Not emission relevant; usually stored without the check engine light.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply wire (chafing)
Relay with internal short (coil bypassed, very low resistance)
Wrong relay fitted
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: A/C not cooling
Compressor clutch never engages
Code stored, check engine light usually off

P0648.title: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
P0648.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. P0648 concerns the immobiliser or security lamp where the engine module drives it directly by wire – on GM and Saab systems this lamp shows the immobiliser learn mode and faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. The lamp then does not show the immobiliser status, or shows it permanently; the immobiliser itself keeps working, because start authorisation is separate (key faults are P0513/P0633). The immobiliser is not an emission component, so no check engine light is expected.

causes.label: Wire or connector between module and receiver open, corroded or shorted
Bulb/LED or instrument cluster faulty
Instrument cluster (board, connector) faulty
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Immobiliser lamp off, permanently on or flashing wrongly
Code stored
Engine start normally not affected

P0649.title: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit
P0649.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. P0649 concerns the cruise control ('speed control') indicator where the engine module drives it by wire. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. CARB names cruise control as an example of a function outside the test cycles, and GM rates its cruise control diagnostics as emission neutral without the check engine light. The indicator then does not work or stays on; whether cruise control is also disabled depends on the maker. Cruise control inputs and switches have their own codes (P0564–P0581).

causes.label: Wire or connector between module and receiver open, corroded or shorted
Bulb/LED or instrument cluster faulty
Instrument cluster faulty
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Cruise control indicator not working or stays on
Cruise control possibly disabled (depending on the maker)
Code stored

P064A.title: Fuel Pump Control Module A
P064A.description: Demand-controlled fuel systems drive the pump through a separate pump control module; the engine module sets the target and reads its status back. P064A means this module reports an internal fault. Ford petrol engines encode the status as a duty cycle on a monitor line – 30 % (±4 %) means internal driver fault, 20 % invalid data (P025B), no signal U0109 – and set the code after 2–5 s; Ford's 2023 diesel checks the period of the monitor signal (0–1.2 s, 0.5 s). GM's pump module sets P064A when its output stage exceeds 150 °C (3 of 15 samples), with the lamp after two trips; Ford petrol stores it without the lamp. Pump output may be reduced or switched off, so low fuel pressure, stalling or a no-start can follow. A stiff, worn pump drawing high current can overheat the module.

causes.label: Pump control module faulty internally (output stage, electronics)
Output stage overheating from a stiff or worn pump or poor module cooling
Supply or ground fault or corrosion at the module (often on frame or tank)
Disturbed monitor line, so a wrong duty cycle is read

symptoms: Check engine light (GM) or stored code only (Ford petrol)
Hard start, stumbling or lack of power from low fuel pressure
Stalling or no start if the pump is switched off
Fuel pressure codes as well (e.g. P0087)

P064B.title: PTO Control Module
P064B.description: A power take-off (PTO) drives equipment on trucks and pick-ups – tipper, crane, hydraulic pump or winch – from the engine or transmission. A PTO control module, or the PTO function in the engine module, manages switching, working speed and release conditions; P064B reports a fault of this module or an implausible PTO request. The only manufacturer document found is a Chrysler case for Ram chassis cabs: with the PTO engaged the engine speed hunts and does not rise above about 1100 rpm, P064B sets together with the torque monitoring code P061B and the PTO switches off; the cause was software, so check upfitter installation and programming before replacing parts. CARB defines PTO units and allows monitors to pause while one is active. Thresholds and lamp status are not published; driving is usually normal.

causes.label: Engine or PTO module software or calibration (implausible torque or speed request)
PTO equipment installed or programmed incorrectly by the upfitter
Harness, connector or supply of the PTO module or switches
PTO control module faulty

symptoms: PTO switches off or cannot be engaged
Engine speed hunts with PTO active or stays below about 1100 rpm (Chrysler)
Warning lamp or stored code; driving usually normal

P064C.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1
P064C.description: On diesels a glow plug control module switches the glow plugs (at Ford also the DEF heaters) with semiconductor switches, diagnoses itself and reports to the engine module. P064C means this module reports an internal fault. GM's 2017–18 Duramax checks for a switch that is commanded on but delivers less than 3.2 A and 0 V at the plug (3.5 s), ROM, RAM and EEPROM checksums, the charge pump of the high-side drivers and reverse polarity; the LML (2011–16) used under 6.6 A for 75 % of 4 s; lamp after two trips. Ford's 2023 diesels flag drivers that do not switch or overheat, a RAM checksum error, supply below 6.5 or above 16.5 V and module temperature above 125 °C, within about 1 s. The glow system then fails partly or completely: hard cold starts, white smoke and higher cold-start emissions.

causes.label: Glow plug module faulty internally (switches, memory)
Insufficient supply or ground (battery, corrosion, main fuse)
Short in a glow plug or wire overloading a driver
Moisture or corrosion in the connector of the engine-mounted module

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in cold weather
White smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug circuit codes as well

P064D.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1
P064D.description: Wide-band oxygen sensors need a pump current control; inside the engine module a dedicated chip (ASIC, for example Bosch's CJ125 family) regulates it, measures lambda, diagnoses sensor wiring and heater, and talks to the main processor via SPI. P064D means this chip for bank 1 sensor 1 does not work correctly or its messages are invalid. Ford validates the SPI communication continuously and sets P064D/P064E after 10 s at 11–18 V with the sensor heater working; an internal chip fault adds Ford's P1646/P1647. GM (wide-band engines such as the 3.0 L twin turbo, 2018–2025) evaluates two error counters from the chip and sets the code at 128 of 160 samples (about 4 s), more than 20 s after start-up, with the lamp after two trips. Fuel control then runs open loop and oxygen sensor monitors are disabled – fuel consumption and emissions rise. Faults in the sensor or wiring can also push the chip into an invalid state.

causes.label: Engine module (lambda chip) faulty
Wiring or sensor fault pushing the chip into an invalid state (short to battery voltage, water in connector)
Faulty wide-band sensor (e.g. heater-to-signal short)
Voltage dips or software

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption, rough running (open loop)
Failed emissions test
Codes for the bank 1 sensor 1 wide-band sensor

P064E.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 2
P064E.description: Wide-band oxygen sensors need a pump current control; inside the engine module a dedicated chip (ASIC, for example Bosch's CJ125 family) regulates it, measures lambda, diagnoses sensor wiring and heater, and talks to the main processor via SPI. P064E is the bank 2 counterpart of P064D and only occurs on V and boxer engines with two sensors before the catalysts. Ford sets it when the SPI communication with the bank 2 chip fails (10 s; an internal chip fault adds Ford's P1647); GM uses the same error counters as for bank 1 (128 of 160 samples, lamp after two trips). Fuel control on bank 2 then runs open loop, with higher consumption and emissions. Check the bank 2 sensor 1 wiring and sensor first; if they are fine, the engine module is the likely cause.

causes.label: Engine module (lambda chip bank 2) faulty
Wiring or connector fault of the bank 2 sensor 1
Bank 2 wide-band sensor faulty
Voltage dips or software

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption, rough running
Failed emissions test
Codes for the bank 2 sensor 1 wide-band sensor

P064F.title: Unauthorized Software/Calibration Detected
P064F.description: P064F means the module has found that its software or calibration is not the version released by the manufacturer, or fails an authenticity check (signature, checksum, security keys). CARB requires manufacturers to protect calibrations against changes without special tools and to report calibration IDs and checksums. GM's 2025 engine modules set it when the embedded message authentication table for secured bus messages is invalid, with the lamp in the first trip; chassis modules also check missing key storage or wrong key-slot configuration. Chrysler fixed P064F on the 2017 Ram 3500–5500 chassis cab 6.7 L Cummins by reprogramming – so it is not only about tuning. Typical triggers are tuning software, an interrupted or wrong reflash, a module from another vehicle, or a module replaced without learning its security keys. Programming released software usually clears it.

causes.label: Unapproved or tuned software (chip tuning, programmer)
Faulty or interrupted reflash, outdated software
Used or replaced module without learning the security keys, wrong configuration
Module faulty internally (key storage)

symptoms: Check engine light (GM in the first trip)
Possibly follow-up codes in other modules or communication problems
Driving often normal

P0650.title: MIL Control Circuit/Open
P0650.description: The engine module switches the check engine light (MIL) through a low-side driver – or sends the command over CAN – and monitors the circuit: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V. CARB requires the MIL to light for a bulb check at ignition on with the engine off (at least 15 s since model year 2005). GM's 2018–2025 modules use P0650 only for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, above 11 V, 50 ms) and P263A/P263B for shorts to ground and voltage – stored without lighting the MIL, since a broken MIL cannot report itself; older GM diesels combine all faults in P0650. GM Europe's Saab 9-5 V6 checks only once the MIL has been commanded on and off. The engine runs normally, but emission faults go unseen and inspections fail if the lamp does not light at the bulb check.

causes.label: Wire or connector between engine module and instrument cluster open or corroded
MIL bulb burnt out or LED/instrument cluster faulty
MIL supply in the cluster missing (fuse, ignition feed)
Short in the circuit (at GM reported as P263A/P263B)
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: MIL does not light at the bulb check
MIL stays on (with a short or combined code)
Code only visible with a scan tool, engine runs normally
Failed emissions inspection

P0651.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit/Open
P0651.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (camshaft, pedal, pressure sensors) from separate regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'B' is circuit 2. A short at one sensor pulls the whole reference down, so every sensor on it reports at once – unplug them one by one until the reference returns to 4.8–5.2 V. P0651 is the general code for circuit B. GM puts all faults into it: reference outside 4.875–5.125 V or jumping, 19 of 39 counts or 0.19 s in a row, with the lamp in the first trip (2018; GM's 2006 V6 used 10 s and two trips). GM Europe's 2.0 L turbo feeds all four camshaft sensors and pedal sensor 1 from it and also uses P0652/P0653 (1 s or 10 s cumulative). Ford reports reference B only as range/performance P06A7. Expect limp mode if the pedal sensor is affected, and starting problems or stalling if camshaft sensors are.

causes.label: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor (camshaft, pedal, pressure)
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A sensor signal wire shorted to voltage
Module internal voltage regulator

symptoms: Check engine light
Several sensor codes at once (camshaft, pedal, pressure)
Limp mode, reduced power
Starting problems or stalling

P0652.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Low
P0652.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (camshaft, pedal, pressure sensors) from separate regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'B' is circuit 2. A short at one sensor pulls the whole reference down, so every sensor on it reports at once – unplug them one by one until the reference returns to 4.8–5.2 V. P0652 means reference B is too low – usually the 5 V line or a connected sensor is shorted to ground. GM's 6.6 L Duramax LB7/LLY (2004–05) sets it below 4.7 V for 2 s; GM Europe's 2.0 L turbo after 1 s or 10 s cumulative, each with the lamp in the first trip. Newer GM engines report it under the collective code P0651, and Ford does not use P0652. All sensors on the circuit then read low, with matching codes, limp mode and possibly starting problems.

Sensor on the reference circuit shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in a connector
Module

symptoms: Check engine light
Several 'low' sensor codes at once
Limp mode or reduced power
Starting problems

P0653.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit High
P0653.description: The engine module feeds several sensors (camshaft, pedal, pressure sensors) from separate regulated 5 V reference circuits; 'B' is circuit 2. A short at one sensor pulls the whole reference down, so every sensor on it reports at once – unplug them one by one until the reference returns to 4.8–5.2 V. P0653 means reference B is too high – often a signal wire of a connected sensor has chafed onto a 12 V line, less often the reference wire itself. GM's Duramax LB7/LLY (2004–05) sets it above 5.2 V for 2 s; GM Europe's 2.0 L turbo after 1 s or 10 s cumulative, each with the lamp in the first trip. Newer GM engines report it as P0651, Ford does not use it. Sensor readings then become implausibly high and limp mode follows.

Module voltage regulator

Several 'high' sensor codes
Limp mode
Implausible sensor values in live data

P0654.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit/Open
P0654.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. P0654 concerns the engine speed output: the module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer and other modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P0654 reports an open circuit or other fault on this output. Saab's EDC16 diesels use P0654 differently (a sensor supply group). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. The tachometer then reads zero or jumps; devices using the signal may fail, while the engine itself runs normally because the crankshaft input is intact.

Output wire shorted
Instrument cluster or receiving module faulty (input stage)
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Tachometer reads zero or jumps
Functions using the speed signal disturbed (accessories, cruise control, shift indicator)
Check engine light depending on the maker

P0655.title: Engine Hot Lamp Output Control Circuit
P0655.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. P0655 concerns the engine hot or coolant warning lamp that the engine module switches by wire from the coolant temperature signal. CARB links overtemperature protection strategies to this lamp: a protective reaction that only starts after the hot lamp lights needs no MIL. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. If the circuit fails, the driver may not be warned of overheating – check it promptly even though the check engine light usually stays off. Actual overheating is P0217; the coolant sensor circuit is P0117/P0118.

Lamp supply missing (fuse)

P0656.title: Fuel Level Output Circuit
P0656.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. Where the engine module reads the fuel level sender itself – it needs the level for the evaporative leak test – it passes the level on to the fuel gauge. GM Europe's 2010 Saab 9-5 reads two senders (0.5–3.5 V), calculates the level in percent and sends it over CAN via the body module to the instrument cluster; there a failure would be a U code. P0656 reports a fault on a hard-wired level output. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. The gauge then reads empty, full or jumps and the low fuel warning is wrong; engine and evaporative test are not affected. Sender input faults are P0460–P0464.

Instrument cluster (fuel gauge input) faulty
Output driver in the module faulty
Fuel level sender fault as root cause

Low fuel warning wrong
Range display wrong

P0657.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit/Open
P0657.description: Actuator supply A is a high-side switch feeding several actuators together; its use differs by maker (Ford transmission solenoids, GM shared high-side driver, GM Europe 2.0 CDTI internal 5 V supply). P0657 is the open-circuit code; it is documented at Ford: the high-side switch of the 5R110W and 6R80 automatics feeds all shift solenoids, and the 2023 diesels split them into two supplies (P0657 and P2669), checked continuously. On a fault the solenoids are de-energised and the transmission falls back to a mechanical limp gear with maximum line pressure – harsh shifts and a single forward gear. Ford's 6.8 L V10 reports it with or without the lamp depending on the variant. GM does not use P0657 and reports opens together with ground faults under P0658.

Damaged harness
Internal high-side switch in the engine or transmission module
Internal transmission harness

symptoms: Transmission limp mode (fixed gear)
Harsh shifts, no upshift
Check engine light (depending on the variant)
Codes for individual shift solenoids

P0658.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Low
P0658.description: Actuator supply A is a high-side switch feeding several actuators together; its use differs by maker (Ford transmission solenoids, GM shared high-side driver, GM Europe 2.0 CDTI internal 5 V supply). P0658 means the supply output is too low with the driver on – a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less). GM's engine module checks its shared high-side driver in 20 of 25 samples; the lamp rating changed from none (2016) via two trips (2017–18) to the first trip (2025). GM's transmission modules include an open circuit here, set it in the first trip and block the solenoid diagnostics, so the gearbox goes into limp mode. On GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI it means the internal 5 V supply is too low – no MIL, and if it recurs, the engine module is replaced.

Actuator (solenoid) shorted internally
Transmission harness or connector (also open, in transmission modules)
Module internal (main cause on the Saab diesel)

Several actuators not working
Check engine light (GM from 2017)
Codes for individual solenoids

P0659.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit High
P0659.description: Actuator supply A is a high-side switch feeding several actuators together; its use differs by maker (Ford transmission solenoids, GM shared high-side driver, GM Europe 2.0 CDTI internal 5 V supply). P0659 means a short to voltage on the supply output, checked with the driver off – the output should then be dead (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to the supply, 20 of 25 samples; lamp after two trips in 2017–18, none in 2016). The driver can then no longer switch the actuators off; GM's transmission modules block their solenoid diagnostics while P0658/P0659 are active, and limp mode follows. On GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI it means the internal 5 V supply is too high, without MIL – the engine module is replaced.

Harness chafed against a 12 V line
Module (driver shorted; internal on the Saab diesel)
External voltage fed back through a faulty actuator

Transmission or actuator limp mode

P065A.title: Generator System Performance
P065A.description: Demand-controlled (smart) charging lets the module vary alternator voltage; the charging system is not an emission component, so these codes usually come without the check engine light. P065A is the function check of the whole charging strategy. Chrysler (Stellantis) explains it as a non-MIL code: the engine module switches off demand-controlled charging and falls back to normal charging because of electrical faults in other modules – returned alternators replaced for P065A were found to be fine. Other Stellantis cases trace it, together with P2503/P2504, to loose B+ or high-current connections, and the Ram 1500 3.0 EcoDiesel Gen 3 received a software update. The result is a constant charging voltage instead of smart charging, possibly with a battery lamp; there is no power limitation. Check codes in other modules and the main battery connections before replacing the alternator.

causes.label: Electrical fault in another module (lighting, wipers, blower) disabling smart charging
Loose or corroded B+ or high-current connection
Engine module software
Alternator or regulator faulty

symptoms: Battery warning lamp (in some cases)
Fluctuating charging voltage reading
No check engine light (Chrysler)
Fault codes in other modules

P065B.title: Generator A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P065B.description: Demand-controlled (smart) charging lets the module vary alternator voltage; the charging system is not an emission component, so these codes usually come without the check engine light. P065B is the plausibility check of the control channel to the alternator regulator (LIN or a dedicated smart-charge line): command and feedback do not match, or the signal is out of range (too low or too high). A manufacturer table published via NHTSA for a gateway with LIN alternator shows the battery lamp and disabled stop-start, notes that jump starting or charging can set it briefly, and says to check P065C (belt) first; Ford's 6.8 L V10 reports it with or without the lamp depending on the variant. The regulator then falls back to a default target voltage. Circuit faults are P0620; L and F lines are P0621/P0622.

causes.label: LIN or control wire between alternator and module (connector, corrosion, open)
Weak battery, jump start or external charging
Alternator regulator faulty
Ground or B+ connections

symptoms: Battery warning lamp on
Stop-start not working
Battery drains
Usually no check engine light

P065C.title: Generator A Mechanical Performance
P065C.description: Demand-controlled (smart) charging lets the module vary alternator voltage; the charging system is not an emission component, so these codes usually come without the check engine light. P065C points to the alternator's mechanical drive: the alternator does not deliver as commanded or its feedback does not match engine speed, typically because the belt slips. The only manufacturer document found – a table for a gateway with LIN alternator published via NHTSA – shows the battery lamp and disabled stop-start and names checking and adjusting the drive belt tension as the fix, to be checked before P065B. Thresholds are not published. Belt wear or oil contamination, a weak tensioner, a faulty overrunning pulley or a stiff alternator bearing are the obvious mechanical causes. Hybrid starter-generators use other codes.

causes.label: Drive belt slipping (tension, wear, oil)
Weak belt tensioner
Alternator overrunning pulley faulty
Alternator bearing or rotor stiff

symptoms: Battery warning lamp
Stop-start disabled
Belt squeal
Low battery voltage

P065D.title: Reductant System Malfunction Lamp Control Circuit
P065D.description: The engine module switches this hard-wired output with its own driver and checks the circuit electrically (open, short to ground or voltage) – it cannot see whether the lamp lights; on CAN-based cars such faults appear as U codes. On SCR diesels a separate lamp or symbol warns of low DEF/AdBlue level, poor quality or system faults and announces speed or start restrictions (inducement). P065D reports a fault in the control circuit of this lamp. CARB requires inputs and outputs of the inducement strategy to be monitored on diesels from model years 2019–2021, and US federal rules define the inducement stages; Detroit Diesel, for example, shows the symbol below 1/8 tank and flashes it with a speed limit when empty. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the component. Without the lamp the driver may run into an inducement stage without warning; the code itself is not known to trigger one.

Bulb/LED or instrument cluster faulty
Lamp supply missing (fuse)
Driver in the engine or SCR module faulty

symptoms: AdBlue warning lamp does not light at ignition on, or stays on
No early warning of low AdBlue (risk of speed limit or no-restart without notice)
Check engine light possible (depending on the maker)

P065E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 1
P065E.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P065E is the function check for bank 1 (or the only valve): the valve does not follow its command. It can be detected with a position sensor or, as a GM patent describes, without one from the intake pressure pulsation in steady running – a closed, tuned manifold pulses more. No manufacturer table available to us uses P065E itself: GM reports the same fault on this valve as P2070/P2071 (end position not reached within 5 s, 320 of 400 samples, two trips), and Ford's valve has no feedback at all. A valve stuck in one position leaves a torque gap in part of the rev range; sooted shafts and broken linkages are typical causes.

causes.label: Valve shaft or linkage stiff or sooted (oil mist from crankcase ventilation or EGR)
Plastic lever or ball joint between actuator and shaft broken or detached
Actuator motor or solenoid faulty (weak, gears)
Manifold leak or, on vacuum-operated actuators, a leak in the vacuum line

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Torque gap in one rev band
Rattling or clicking from the intake manifold
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P065F.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 2
P065F.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P065F is the function check of the bank 2 valve: it does not follow its command, detected via a position sensor or the intake pressure pulsation (GM patent). Bank 2 codes require a V-engine manifold with two separately switched valves; many V engines use a single central valve between the plenums, and no manufacturer document available to us uses this code, so the description follows bank 1. A stuck valve causes a torque gap in one rev band and can make the banks fill unevenly. Bank 2 circuit faults are P0663–P0665.

Torque gap in one rev band
Noise from the intake manifold

P0660.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P0660.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0660 means the control circuit of the bank 1 (or only) valve is open. GM evaluates the line voltage with the driver off: too low means the supply through the coil is missing (200 kΩ or more). GM's engines with this valve (low-side driver) check with ignition voltage of at least 11 V and the engine above 400 rpm and set the code after 40 of 50 samples (about 0.6 s), with the check engine light after two trips. Ford uses P0660 (older: P1549) as the electrical check of its actuator, which has no position feedback and stays closed and unpowered below about 2600 rpm – without the check engine light (5 s). The valve then stays in its rest position and power at high revs suffers.

Broken or chafed wire (control or supply)
Supply (fuse, main relay) to the actuator missing
Output driver in the engine module faulty

P0661.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P0661.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0661 means the bank 1 control circuit voltage is too low with the driver off – a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less), which bypasses the driver and keeps the valve energised; GM also includes an open circuit (200 kΩ or more) here, so P0660 may set alongside. GM's engines with this valve (low-side driver) check with ignition voltage of at least 11 V and the engine above 400 rpm and set the code after 40 of 50 samples (about 0.6 s), with the check engine light after two trips. P0662.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 1
P0662.description: The intake manifold tuning valve switches the manifold length or plenum connection with engine speed (more torque low, more power high); it is not the runner or swirl flap (IMRC, P2004 ff). P0664.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 2

P0665.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 2

P0666.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0666.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0666 is the general circuit fault of this sensor A. No manufacturer table available to us uses P0666 itself – GM splits the circuit faults into low (P0668) and high (P0669), plausibility is P0667. P0667.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
P0667.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0667 is the plausibility check: GM compares the module (substrate) temperature with the transmission fluid temperature and the temperature measured at power-up. The module then uses the power-up temperature instead. Check the fluid temperature sensor (P0711) first – it is the comparison partner.

P0668.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0668.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. In GM's 6T70/6T75 and related automatics the sensor sits in the transmission module inside the valve body, with no external wiring – so the repair is practically always the module or valve body assembly. P0668 means the sensor signal is at the low voltage end: GM converts it into a temperature and treats −249 °C or less – a physically impossible value – for 60 s as a fault, with the lamp after two trips and the power-up temperature as substitute. P0669.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0669.description: Control modules measure their own circuit board temperature with an internal sensor to protect output stages (overtemperature is P0634) and, in GM transmission modules, as a substitute for fluid temperature. P06C5.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Incorrect
P06C5.description: A glow plug has no identification; the control unit recognises its type only from its electrical behaviour – cold resistance at switch-on and how resistance rises during heating (R = U/I). A Beru patent describes how steel and ceramic plugs are told apart this way so the right heating profile is used and a wrong or mixed type is reported. A low-voltage plug on an 11 V control burns out, an 11 V plug on a low-voltage control glows too weakly. GM uses 'incorrect' for any resistance outside the window: the 2025 diesels check 0.22–2.00 Ω (15 of 25 samples, two trips), the L5P glow module a ramp-dependent window. P06C5 reports this for cylinder 1. VW's 2.0 TDI (Jetta, Golf, Passat 2011–13) checks the type 2 s after ignition on – starting during that time caused false codes from the voltage dip, fixed with new glow module software.

causes.label: Wrong glow plug type fitted in cylinder 1 (steel/ceramic, voltage rating)
Plug resistance drifted (ageing, damage)
Glow module software or check during cranking (false report)
Contact resistance at the plug connector

No manufacturer document available to us names P06D8 itself; Ram's 6.7 L Cummins documents the neighbouring P06D3. Sensors on the circuit then read too high.

causes.label: Reference or sensor signal wire shorted to 12 V
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A connected sensor faulty internally
Module internal voltage regulator or components

symptoms: Check engine light
Several sensor codes at once
Reduced power or limp mode
Possibly starting problems

P06D9.title: Sensor Reference Voltage F Circuit Range/Performance

causes.label: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A connected sensor faulty internally
Module internal voltage regulator or components

symptoms: Check engine light
Several sensor codes at once
Reduced power or limp mode
Possibly starting problems

P06DA.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit/Open
P06DA.description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DA means the control circuit of this valve is open: it can no longer be powered, so the pump stays at high pressure. GM measures the voltage with the driver off and flags more than 200 kΩ after two trips; some GM modules set P06DB instead. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander uses the same code. The engine is not at risk, the pump just can no longer be regulated.

causes.label: Connector at the control valve loose or corroded (often at the pump in the oil pan)
Valve coil open or valve broken
Supply (main relay) or control wire broken
Engine module software

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable symptom, oil pressure permanently high
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P06DB.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Low
P06DB.description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DB means the control wire behind the valve is shorted to ground. With a low-side driver the valve is then powered all the time, so the pump stays at the low stage even at high load and speed. That endangers the engine, so GM flags a short below 0.5 Ω after just one trip, unlike open circuit and short to positive. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. A short to positive is P06DC, a pump stuck at low pressure without a circuit fault P06DE.

causes.label: Control wire chafing against ground (engine block, oil pan)
Control valve shorted internally
Oil or moisture in the connector
Engine module driver stage

symptoms: Check engine light at once (GM after one trip)
Low oil pressure at high engine speed, possibly oil pressure warning
Possibly reduced power

P06DC.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit High
P06DC.description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. P06DD.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P06DD.description: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; unpowered it delivers high pressure. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DD means the pressure does not react and stays above the threshold – the pump acts as if the valve were stuck off, at high pressure; GM sets it after two trips. Yet GM bulletins for V8 and 2.5 L engines list P06DD with low oil pressure, too: broken valve tips, unseated valves, a loose pump drive gear or worn tensioners also stop the pressure from changing. Check oil level and pressure before replacing parts.

causes.label: Control valve stuck or broken, screen clogged
Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludge
Mechanical pump or drive damage (tensioner, drive gear, pump face)
Valve not seated correctly (retaining clip)
Oil pressure sensor inaccurate

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Oil pressure stays high – or, with pump damage, low or fluctuating
Possibly oil pressure warning
Slightly higher fuel consumption

P06DE.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck On
P06DE.description: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; powered it runs at the low stage. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DE is the counterpart of P06DD: the commanded high stage is not reached and the pressure stays below the threshold, as if the valve were stuck on. Too little oil pressure at high load endangers the engine, so GM sets it after just one trip; a Ford patent raises idle speed in this case. A short to ground on the control wire (P06DB) has the same effect electrically. An FCA bulletin for the 3.6 L V6 fixes false codes by software.

causes.label: Control valve stuck in the powered position
Low oil level, diluted or sludged oil, aeration
Pump wear or internal leakage
Engine module software (FCA 3.6 L)
Oil pressure sensor

symptoms: Check engine light at once
Oil pressure warning at higher engine speed possible
Possibly reduced power or raised idle
Valvetrain or chain tensioner noise from lack of oil

P06DF.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Memory Checksum Error
P06DF.description: A diesel glow plug control module has its own microcontroller. On power-up it forms a checksum over its memory and compares it with the stored value; P06DF means they differ, so the module's program or data cannot be trusted. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06DF among the glow module checks, run at power-up and flagged on a RAM checksum mismatch after about 1 s. GM's L5P performs the same check on ROM (4.5 s, two trips) but reports it as P064C. CARB treats the module as a 'smart device' whose internal faults need not be pinpointed, so this is extra diagnosis by the manufacturer. The usual remedy is reprogramming or replacing the module; until then preheating may be missing.

causes.label: Glow plug control module faulty internally (memory, controller)
Failed or interrupted programming of the module
Voltage dip or spike at power-up (weak battery, poor ground)
Moisture or corrosion in module or connector

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking
White smoke and knocking after cold start
Often no symptoms when warm

P06E0.title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P06E0.description: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E0 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag below 0.11 Ω to ground after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke more than 22 A for 0.3 s or 20–22 A for 2 s while heating. The channel is switched off and the plug stays cold; the other plugs keep working. An internally shorted plug or a chafed wire is the usual cause. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.

causes.label: Cylinder 11 glow plug shorted internally
Plug wire chafed through to ground
Burnt connector or terminal nut, tracking through oil or moisture
Driver stage in the glow module defective

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Harder cold start in frost
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start
Cylinder 11 misfire when cold

P06E1.title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P06E1.description: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E1 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to positive: voltage is present although the driver is off, or no current flows when it is on. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag a short to positive below 0.5 Ω after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke 0 A while commanded for about 1 s. The plug may glow permanently and fail early; the other plugs keep working. Wiring shorted to supply or a failed driver are the usual causes. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.

Glow module software

P06E4.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Performance
P06E4.description: Control modules are woken by a dedicated wake-up line or a network wake-up – at ignition on, when a charging cable is plugged in, or on a timer for engine-off diagnostics and battery management. P06E4 means this wake-up signal is implausible: the module wakes too late or not at all, stays awake, or the line state does not match the network status. In practice the code appears mainly on hybrids: FCA fixes it on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and the Wrangler 4xe with module software, where it remained as a permanent code that blocked emission inspections; GM's hybrid integration module lists it as a fault bundle. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or timing.

causes.label: Module software (false setting, permanent code does not clear)
Wake-up line or connector open or shorted
Weak 12 V battery, voltage dips at wake-up

symptoms: Check engine light
Permanent code blocks emission inspection

P06E5.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Performance
P06E5.description: P06E5 means glow plug control module 1 does not respond correctly to the glow command: its outputs do not switch or its internal drivers report faults or overheating. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06E5 among the glow module checks, run continuously, with a fault after about 1 s when internal drivers for glow plugs, DEF heaters or relays fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s – Ford does not assign each threshold to a single code. GM files the same check under P064C: on the L5P a plug commanded on but drawing under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s, on the LML a total current under 6.6 A; both after two trips. The plugs then heat partly or not at all, with hard cold starts and white smoke. There is no limp mode.

Poor supply or ground of the module (main feed, fuse, ground)
Module overheating (mounting location, short at a plug)
Module software

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking
White smoke and rough running after cold start
Often stored together with plug codes or P064C/P263C

P06E6.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit/Open
P06E6.description: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit. P06E6 is the general or open-circuit code of supply C: the module measures the output of its supply regulator and finds the voltage missing. Low and high are P06E7/P06E8. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P06E6 as a main code with sub-codes for low and high, called internal control module, without thresholds or the sensors fed. All sensors on the circuit then deliver invalid values, so several follow-up codes and limp mode are possible.

causes.label: Open circuit or connector problem in the supply circuit
Short in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Vehicle under- or overvoltage

symptoms: Check engine light
Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E7.description: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. P06E9.title: Engine Starter Performance
P06E9.description: On cars with stop-start or keyless start the engine module operates the starter relay itself and watches the start: if cranking is commanded but the engine does not turn, turns too slowly or the start is aborted, it sets P06E9. CARB counts an engine start from 150 rpm below warm idle. Thresholds for speed and time are not published. Bulletins show both sides: VW traces P06E9 on the Tiguan to dirt inside the starter that opens its contacts intermittently, and on the Atlas has relays, battery and voltage drop checked; Audi's SQ5 and FCA's Jeep Compass need module software instead. Ford lists P06E9 among the starter faults that disable stop-start.

causes.label: Starter worn or solenoid contacts intermittently open
Weak battery, voltage drop on main cables or ground
Starter relay or its control
Engine module software

symptoms: Intermittent no-start or only clicking
Stop-start not working
Check engine light depending on manufacturer (FCA: yes)
Long cranking

P06EA.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P06EA.description: A modern NOx sensor is a smart sensor: a ceramic sensing element with pump cells and heater plus its own control unit with a microcontroller, which regulates the pump currents, calculates NOx and oxygen and sends them to the engine module over CAN. P06EA means this control unit of sensor 1 (before the SCR catalyst) reports an internal fault – its self-tests of RAM and ROM or EEPROM checksums fail – so the electronics, not the sensing element, are at fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: Ford's 2023 diesels run exactly these checks continuously, with a fault after 5 s, but report them as P2200; GM uses the P2200 family and U029D/U029E. The NOx value is then invalid, so SCR dosing runs on a model or stops, a warning appears and, depending on market, a countdown to a start lock.

causes.label: Faulty electronics in the NOx sensor control unit
Moisture or corrosion in control unit or connector (underbody location)
Under- or overvoltage or dips in the sensor supply
Unsuitable replacement sensor or software

symptoms: Check engine light or emissions warning
Message to check AdBlue/emission system, possibly countdown to start lock
Follow-up codes for SCR efficiency or NOx plausibility
Driveability usually unchanged

P06EC.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P06EC.description: P06EC is a notice code like P0700: a separate fuel injector control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module over CAN to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault is stored in that module and must be read there; simple OBD readers show only P06EC. GM uses it on the 2019 Corvette ZR1, whose LT5 engine adds port injection driven by its own module with its own crank and cam inputs; the code runs continuously from key on and is listed as type A without its own MIL – the lamp comes from the module's fault. Older separate injector modules (Ford 6.0 L Power Stroke, GM bi-fuel CNG trucks) report through P0611 or U codes instead. Any limp mode follows the module's fault.

causes.label: Emission-related fault in the injector control module or its injectors/sensors (code stored there)
Supply, ground or relay problem of the module
Internal module fault (memory, processor)
Software level of engine or injector module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Generic scanner shows only P06EC – details in the injector module

P06ED.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Low
P06ED.description: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P06ED means this output is too low, typically shorted to ground, so it can no longer switch high. It is the counterpart of P0654 (open circuit) and P06EE (high). CARB requires output circuits to be checked; the signal is emission-relevant only if a receiving module uses it for emission functions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB, the component and P0654. The tachometer then reads zero or jumps, and modules using the signal lose it, while the engine runs normally.

causes.label: Speed output wire chafing against ground
Receiver (instrument, add-on device) shorted internally
Aftermarket tachometer or accessory wired wrongly
Engine module driver stage

symptoms: Tachometer at zero or jumping
Other modules without speed signal
Engine runs normally

P06EE.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit High
P06EE.description: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. causes.label: Output wire shorted to 12 V
Wrongly connected accessory (speed pick-up)
Receiving device faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Tachometer shows nothing or full scale
Other modules without speed signal

P06EF.title: Engine Restart Performance
P06EF.description: P06EF concerns the automatic restart after the system itself has stopped the engine – stop-start or hybrid. The restart, by starter, reinforced stop-start starter or belt starter-generator, takes too long or fails. CARB does not count such a commanded shutdown as a stall. No manufacturer publishes the time limit. VW's Tiguan bulletins list P06EF together with P06E9 and trace both to dirt inside the starter; FCA fixes it on the 2019 Jeep Wrangler with engine-module software and lights the check engine light. Stop-start is then disabled. Besides the starter, a weak stop-start battery or fuel and ignition problems at restart can be the cause.

causes.label: Starter or starter-generator worn, contacts intermittently open
Engine module software
Weak stop-start battery (AGM/EFB) or battery sensor
Fuel pressure or ignition at restart

symptoms: Engine does not restart or restarts late after stop-start
Stop-start disabled
Check engine light (FCA)

P06F0.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P06F0.description: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat. P06F0 is the general circuit fault of this internal sensor: the signal is missing, open or cannot be evaluated. Range, low and high are P06F1–P06F3; the DEF tank temperature sensor is a different part. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06F0–P06F3; Ford and GM report related faults under P20FF or own codes. Without a valid temperature the module limits or stops heaters and pump, so dosing is restricted and an SCR warning, up to a start lock countdown, may follow.

causes.label: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)
Driveability usually unchanged

P06F3.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P06F3.description: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat. P06F3 means the signal is above its maximum; with the usual NTC voltage divider that is an open circuit or short to positive, and the reading appears implausibly cold. The opposite fault is P06F2, an implausible reading P06F1. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06F0–P06F3; Ford and GM report related faults under P20FF or own codes. Without a valid temperature the module limits or stops heaters and pump, so dosing is restricted and an SCR warning, up to a start lock countdown, may follow.

causes.label: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)
Driveability usually unchanged

P06F4.title: Stop-Start Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06F4.description: When the engine module switches a lamp through its own wire, it checks the output driver electrically like other lamp outputs: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V – GM's MIL driver, for example, flags an open circuit at 200 kΩ or more. It cannot see whether the bulb lights, and on cars that send the lamp command over CAN such faults appear as U codes. P06F4 concerns the indicator showing that stop-start is active or disabled; the code reports a fault in its control circuit. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the description follows CARB's output check and other lamp circuits. Only the display is affected – the stop-start function itself has its own codes (P06E9, P06EF).

causes.label: Wire or connector to the indicator open or shorted
Indicator or instrument cluster faulty
Engine module driver stage

symptoms: Stop-start indicator not working or permanently lit
Usually no check engine light

P06F5.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2
P06F5.description: SAE J2012 provides a complete code family for a second glow plug control module, mirroring module 1 code for code. P06F5 is the general or internal fault of module 2, the counterpart of P064C. For module 1, GM's L5P groups driver faults (under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s) and a ROM checksum error under P064C, after two trips; Ford's 2023 Power Stroke lists P064C among the module checks with detection in about 1 s. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P064C). The plugs fed by module 2 then heat poorly or not at all.

causes.label: Glow plug control module 2 faulty internally
Poor supply or ground of module 2
Module software or configuration

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06F6.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit/Open
P06F6.description: P06F6 means the command line from the engine module to glow plug control module 2 is open or has a general circuit fault – the counterpart of P0670 for module 1. The engine module's output driver detects an open load while the driver is off. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P0670). Shorts on the same line are P06F7 (to ground) and P06F8 (to positive); the feedback line back to the engine module is P06FC/P06FD. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Line from engine module to glow module 2 open, connector loose or corroded
Input of glow module 2 faulty or module not connected
Engine module output driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06F7.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit Low
P06F7.description: P06F7 means the command line from the engine module to glow plug control module 2 is too low, typically shorted to ground – the counterpart of P0383 for module 1. The engine module's output driver detects the short by its current when switched on or by the line voltage when switched off. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P0383). An open line is P06F6, a short to positive P06F8. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Command line to glow module 2 chafed through to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the connector bridging to ground
Input of glow module 2 or engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06F8.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit High
P06F8.description: P06F8 means the command line from the engine module to glow plug control module 2 is too high, typically shorted to positive – the counterpart of P0384 for module 1. Note that Ford's 2023 diesels use P0384 differently, for the supply voltage of the glow module (below 6.5 V or above 16.5 V); in J2012 that is P052F, and for module 2 P06F9. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P0384). An open line is P06F6, a short to ground P06F7. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Command line shorted to positive or supply
Corrosion in the connector bridging to a B+ pin
Engine module driver shorted

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06F9.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 System Voltage
P06F9.description: P06F9 means the supply voltage of glow plug control module 2 is out of range – the counterpart of P052F for module 1. For module 1, Ford's 2023 Power Stroke flags below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or an open supply after about 1 s; GM's L5P checks the same under P163C (below 6.0 V with ignition above 9 V, or implausible against ignition voltage, 4 s). An FCA bulletin shows P052F together with the glow plug open codes, because without supply no current flows. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P052F). Check main feed, fuses and ground first.

causes.label: Main feed to glow module 2 open or high-resistance (fuse, fusible link, B+ wire)
Weak battery or discharged auxiliary battery
Module ground corroded
Charging voltage too high

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06FA.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Performance
P06FA.description: P06FA means glow plug control module 2 does not respond correctly to the glow command – the counterpart of P06E5 for module 1. For module 1, Ford's 2023 Power Stroke flags internal drivers that fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s; GM's L5P files the same check under P064C (under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s, two trips). No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P06E5). Internal checksum errors are P06FB, overheating P263F. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Glow module 2 faulty internally (drivers do not switch)
Poor supply or ground of module 2
Module overheating
Module software

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06FB.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Memory Checksum Error
P06FB.description: P06FB means glow plug control module 2 has found a memory checksum error – the counterpart of P06DF for module 1. The module forms a checksum over its memory at power-up and compares it with the stored value. For module 1, Ford's 2023 Power Stroke checks the RAM checksum at power-up (about 1 s); GM's L5P checks the ROM checksum (4.5 s, two trips) and reports it as P064C. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P06DF). The usual remedy is reprogramming or replacing the module. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Glow module 2 faulty internally (memory)
Interrupted programming or faulty software
Voltage dip at power-up

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06FC.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit
P06FC.description: P06FC means the feedback or communication from glow plug control module 2 to the engine module is missing, or the line is open or shorted – the counterpart of P0683 for module 1. Depending on design the module reports over a single feedback wire (Bosch-type systems expect it inverse to the command line) or over the bus; GM and Ford report a lost bus link as U0106 rather than P0683. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P0683). The engine module then loses the plug status reports; implausible messages are P06FD. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Feedback or bus line open or shorted, connector corroded
Glow module 2 without supply (does not transmit)
Glow module 2 or engine module interface faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06FD.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit Range/Performance
P06FD.description: P06FD means signals or messages from glow plug control module 2 arrive at the engine module but are implausible – wrong duty cycle or pattern, feedback not matching the command, or single messages timing out. It is the counterpart of P0684 for module 1; Saab's Bosch-based diesels, for example, expect the feedback signal to be inverse to the command line. No manufacturer document available to us uses a second glow module – Ford's and GM's V8 diesels drive all eight plugs from one; the code suits systems with one module per cylinder bank. The description follows module 1 (P0684). A missing signal or open line is P06FC, a lost bus link usually U0106. The plugs of module 2 then heat poorly or not at all, typically on one bank.

causes.label: Loose contact or contact resistance in the feedback or bus line
Ground offset between module and engine module from glow currents
Software mismatch between modules or module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only
Usually no symptoms when warm

P06FE.title: Cold Start Diesel Intake Air Flow Control Performance
P06FE.description: 'Diesel intake air flow control' is the diesel's electric intake throttle with position sensor (P02E0 ff). During cold start many diesels close it partly: the extra load raises exhaust temperature so the catalysts light off sooner. CARB requires such cold start elements to be monitored, with their own codes separate from normal operation. P06FE means the throttle does not reach its target position while the cold start strategy is active – it is not the intake air heater. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06FE: GM's 2025 diesels run this check under P2957 (deviation above 16 % or 10 %, two trips), Ford's 2023 diesels under P02E4 in cold start mode. Cold start emissions rise; driveability usually stays normal.

causes.label: Intake throttle coked with soot and oil (EGR, crankcase ventilation)
Throttle motor or gear stiff, position sensor faulty
Ice or condensate in the intake in frost
Contact resistance in connector or wiring, low voltage

symptoms: Check engine light, usually after two trips
Hardly any change in driveability
Possibly more smoke or smell while warming up
Further throttle codes (P02E1/P02E4/P02E5) possible

P06FF.title: Economy Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06FF.description: When the engine module switches a lamp through its own wire, it checks the output driver electrically like other lamp outputs: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V – GM's MIL driver, for example, flags an open circuit at 200 kΩ or more. It cannot see whether the bulb lights, and on cars that send the lamp command over CAN such faults appear as U codes. P06FF concerns an economy indicator such as an ECO lamp that the engine module switches directly; the code reports a fault in its control circuit. It should not be confused with a body electrics 'economy mode' that saves battery energy. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's output check and other lamp circuits. Driving is not affected.

causes.label: Wire or connector to the lamp open or shorted
Lamp or instrument cluster faulty
Engine module

symptoms: ECO indicator not working or permanently lit
No effect on driving
